### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2555b629e0d61b225208911ba28303ce9d6129f9` — the merge of head `d493e22573327f0ffbf138004f45c70b16b28a02` into base `d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2555b629e0d61b225208911ba28303ce9d6129f9 && git checkout 2555b629e0d61b225208911ba28303ce9d6129f9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038 d493e22573327f0ffbf138004f45c70b16b28a02 && git checkout -B drift-repro d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038 && git merge --no-ff d493e22573327f0ffbf138004f45c70b16b28a02

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d48931871479ccc303e10493e80799225b220038` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d493e22573327f0ffbf138004f45c70b16b28a02`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #15204 (body and all 109 comments, the U2 measurement 6106844492, the claim amendment 6108623383 and the build report 6109851687 among them), PR #22854 (body, 23-file list, net diff against `main` at `d493e22`; branch `claude/issue-15204-su2-suggestion-confirm`, cloud dev `session_01D4f5gJKWdzmeZP57AVkRJd`), decision card #22801 with ruling record 6108478638 (A), and the check-runs on `d493e22`. Head files were read through `contents?ref=d493e22` for context only (`security-plugin.ts`, `index.ts`, `builtin-positions.ts`, `cleanup-package-permissions.ts`, `package.json`). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each line names a change the diff implies, then judges it against the ruling's quoted sentence or the rule that governs it.

1. **The accept takes effect** — ruling: "reaches every signed-in user only through ONE explicit, deployment-level acceptance by an admin holding `manage_metadata`, and that acceptance takes effect." `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` writes `status: confirmed, deployment_decision: true` on the Default Organization's row, then `deps.rederiveEveryone()` runs `SecurityPlugin.declareEveryone`, which re-registers `everyone` through `declareEveryoneBaseline(ql.registry, SECURITY_PLUGIN_ID, baseline + accepted)` and bumps the metadata epoch. The dogfood pin measures a member's read going 403 to 200, the definition still declared by `com.objectstack.plugin-security`, no `sys_metadata` shadow, and `PUT /meta/position/everyone` still 403. **Right.**
2. **Where it re-derives** — ruling: "recomputes it on accept, uninstall and publish." The diff runs `declareEveryone` at `kernel:ready`, on confirm, on dismiss-as-revoke, after `cleanupPackagePermissions` on uninstall, and in the permission publish materializer after the reconcile. **Right**, with one inherited condition carried in ③ (flag A).
3. **The high-risk gate sits on the definition** — ruling: "The definition side carries the high-risk gate (ADR-0090 D7)." The accept asks `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(entry.definition, 'everyone', declaredCapabilityContext)` and refuses `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` asks the same predicate again on every derivation and withholds a set that fails it (logged at `error`), as it withholds a set the catalog no longer serves, serves under another package, or that no longer declares `isDefault` (logged at `warn`). The old second line of defence, the junction-insert middleware, had nothing left to guard; asking the gate at accept and at every derivation closes the accept-then-widen-by-publish hole instead. **Right.**
4. **Reconciliation reads the definition** — ruling sentence verbatim. "Observed" is now `everyoneDefinitionSets(ql).has(set)` through `securityCatalogReaderOf(ql).resolve('position', 'everyone')`. No read of `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` or `sys_position_permission_set` remains in the module at the head, and neither `readDeclared` nor `upsertPackagePermissionSet` is imported: what 6b-2 and stage 8 need is delivered. **Right.**
5. **The record is the Default Organization's** — ruling: "The acceptance record belongs to the default organization." `resolveDefaultOrganizationId` (slug `default`, else the only organization) is plugin-auth's boot derivation read-only; every read and write carries `{ isSystem: true, tenantId }` and is filtered by `ownedBy`, which drops the ADR-0120 D3 NULL-bucket rows; with no owner the surface answers `409 SUGGESTION_STATE` naming the remedy. Boot order checked at the head: under `single` plugin-auth creates the organization in `start()` (before `kernel:ready`); the security plugin registers the derivation hook in its `start()` before `runBootstrap`'s hook, so accepted rows are derived before the reconcile reads the definition, and the reconcile skips `deployment_decision` rows. **Right.**
6. **Authority** — ruling: "an admin holding `manage_metadata`", "Under a wall, only the platform operator" (#22621 to A, ADR-0126 section 5). `assertDeploymentAuthority` on all three routes: `isSystem` passes; no `userId` is 403; `systemPermissions` without `manage_metadata` (`METADATA_AUTHORING_CAPABILITY`) is 403; `postureEnforcesWall(posture)` with `callerCtx.posture !== 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` is 403, read off the execution context's posture rung and never a position name. This is the accept-set narrowing for the tenant administrator (the ADR-0066 wildcard holder), on list, confirm and dismiss alike. **Right**; the list's inclusion is judged in ③ (question 4).
7. **Confirm refusals** — a `guest`-anchor row is 409 (new); a set the catalog does not serve, serves under another package (ADR-0086 D4) or that no longer declares `isDefault` is 409 (replacing the old "not materialized" and "owned by another package" 409s); a non-pending row stays 409. Each refusal case in the unit suite asserts `code` and `statusCode`. **Right.**
8. **Dismiss** — a pending row is dismissed as before (now with `deployment_decision: true`); an accepted row is revoked and `everyone` re-derived without the set (new, same path and envelope); an observed baseline row is 409 with the reason; a dismissed row is 409. The pin measures revoke taking the member back to 403. **Right.**
9. **Rows written before this PR** — a Default Organization row resolved without `deployment_decision` is re-opened to `pending` (or marked observed when the definition names the set); rows owned by another organization or by none are counted as `unread`, warned once per reconcile, never read, never promoted, never deleted. This is #22601 to B (no transition piece) and the dispatch's "never promote a tenant administrator's confirm". **Right.**
10. **Public TypeScript surface of `@objectstack/plugin-security`** — `index.ts` removes `reapOrganizationLessSuggestions`, `listSuggestionOrganizationIds` and the `SuggestionReconcileScope` type and adds `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` and `WithheldAcceptance`; `reconcileAudienceBindingSuggestions(ql, logger)` and `syncAudienceBindingSuggestions(ql, logger)` lose their metadata, scope and organization parameters; `SuggestionDeps` drops `resolveSets` and takes `posture` and `rederiveEveryone`; `SuggestionReconcileOutcome` reports `unread` for `organizations` and `reaped`; `SuggestionSyncOutcome` gains `reopened`. No other importer exists in the repository (grep at `main`: the module, its test, the index and the object). `collectDeclaredSuggestions` (now async) and `resolveDefaultOrganizationId` are module exports the index does not re-export, so they are not public. Every public move is named in the changeset. **Right.**
11. **Stored shape** — `sys_audience_binding_suggestion.deployment_decision`, boolean, `defaultValue: false`, readonly; the per-organization unique key on `(package_id, permission_set_name, anchor)` is unchanged. Additive. **Right.**
12. **Wire shape** — paths and envelopes unchanged, `{ data: { suggestions, synced } }` and `{ data: { suggestion, bindingCreated } }`; `synced` gains `reopened`. Additive. **Right**; the consumer consequence is carried in ③ (flag C).
13. **The spec texts are kept and made true** — `confirmAudienceBindingSuggestion` still says "writes the binding", the package-level `isDefault` note still says "an admin confirms in Setup", each now stating the mechanism; `listAudienceBindingSuggestions` names the `manage_metadata` gate. No Zod shape changes; Spec property liveness is green on the head. The client TSDoc, the REST route summaries, the runtime header and the cli inventory citation follow the same sentence. **Right.**
14. **ADR-0090 D5 stands unchanged** — no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` path in the file list; Governed Surface Queue Guard green. The 2c "sealed" reading ("an acceptance changes the input of a derivation, and no caller writes the anchor's definition") is written into `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` beside the door, and the changeset repeats it. **Right.**
15. **Tests and ledgers** — the install-path suite (557 lines; its subject, per-organization rows, is what the ruling retires) is deleted with its two `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` rows; the unit suite is rewritten for the deployment-level record; the dogfood pin boots a vanilla `SecurityPlugin` so the showcase's own set is a package suggestion; the tenant-audit census is regenerated (233 to 231: the junction insert and one suggestion delete retired) with its prose counts corrected; `system-context.mdx` row 57 is re-anchored to `assertDeploymentAuthority`; checklist item `access-security.suggested-binding-loop` is revision 3 with its history row. **Right.** (`check:platform-checklist` is kept out of per-PR CI by maintainer decision, `lint.yml`; its seven pre-existing reds on `main` are the watchdog's, not this PR's.)
16. **Gate verdicts on `d493e22`** (the check-runs, read immediately before this record was posted): 27 completed, none failed — success on Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3, 3/3 and the roll-up), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check (source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, workspace, and the roll-up), filter; skipped by path filter on Console Pin Gate and Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in). **Seven were still in progress when this record was written: Lint & Repo Gates and Test Core 1/6 through 6/6.** The judgments above are judgments of the diff and do not depend on them; the owning seat reads those seven before queueing, and the Tier S landing rule (every check green) already refuses a landing over a red one. The dev's local battery at this head reports Lint's repo gates and the Test Core packages green (report 6109851687), which this record does not re-run.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15204-su2-suggestion-acceptance.md` — `@objectstack/plugin-security` **minor**, body `**BREAKING**`, summary `feat(plugin-security)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, adr-0087 marker `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts#SuggestionDeps, ...#SuggestionReconcileOutcome)`. **Right on all four counts.** The diff removes exports and narrows a published REST authority, so it is breaking; this repository spells a breaking changeset `minor` plus banner outside pre-mode (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, as `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` records), and that gate's own fixtures read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` as the breaking declaration of "a diff that widens AND narrows" (#16421), which is this diff: the accept now grants, and the caller set and the export set shrink. The D7 disposition fits: the moved symbols are runtime TypeScript interfaces with no Zod schema, no spec declaration and no stored representation `objectstack migrate meta` could rewrite; the one stored change is an additive column with a default; the only authored-metadata text touched is TSDoc. The arrow-form FROM/TO block is refused beside this category (ADR-0087 addendum, the disposition table: `runtime-interface-only` "inherits that same refusal"), and the body carries the migration in substance — each removed symbol named with "nothing replaces them", each changed signature named with its new shape, the tenant-administrator narrowing stated as before and now with its remedy — which is the text an upgrading agent greps after the compiler names the caller.
- `.changeset/15204-su2-contract-text.md` — `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/cli` **patch**, `Clause-②: no`. **Right**: TSDoc, SDK doc comments, route summaries and one inventory citation string; no accept set moves in those packages.
- `@objectstack/runtime` — a header comment; no changeset. **Right**: it publishes nothing. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- `Clause-②:` line — the PR body's second line reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; it matches the dispatch's `Clause-②: yes` and the breaking changeset's own line, and one arm from the closed pair is declared. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations (6, report 6109851687)** — each answered:
1. FROM/TO block vs ADR-0087 D7 — the accepted ADR binds (Prime Directive 13), the mapping is carried in substance (② above), no ledger entry is owed. Closed.
2. Census and system-context pages regenerated outside the dispatch's landing zone — both are generated or pinned pages this diff made false, and both gates run per PR in `lint.yml`; carrying them here is the only correct place. Closed.
3. cli inventory citation corrected — published text, covered by the patch changeset. Closed.
4. `os-regen-merge.sh` took `main`'s side of `system-context.mdx`; row 57 re-applied by hand — the head carries the row and the census gate verifies it. Closed.
5. Model-free commit trailers — process, not contract; AGENTS.md's spelling. Noted, no action.
6. One cli unit flake under the gate battery's load, green alone and in the final full run — not a contract matter; Test Core on the head is the answer. Noted.

**Open questions (4)** — each answered on the record:
1. `guest` suggestions refused `409` rather than derived — **right.** Zero producers; the `guest` anchor's sets are assembled by name, not derived, so an accepted `guest` row would be a declared grant the runtime never delivers (declared must equal enforced); no new capability. ADR-0138 section 5 names a path this head does not have; the dev's #22619 carrier holds it. Not escalated.
2. Revoke is a dismiss on an accepted row — **right.** Same path and envelope, no new route, and it removes the only-undo-is-uninstall gap a deployment-wide widening would otherwise leave; an observed baseline row stays refused. Not escalated.
3. Legacy rows: `deployment_decision` flag, re-open the Default Organization's, leave the others unread and warned — **right.** Never promotes a tenant administrator's past confirm, needs no migration piece (#22601 to B), keeps the audit history. Not escalated.
4. The list takes the same authority as confirm and dismiss — **right.** The list reconciles, so it writes the deployment's record, and a reader who cannot decide would otherwise read decisions; one authority for the surface keeps the read as strict as the write, as before. The consequence for objectui is flag C. Not escalated.

**Reviewer's flags (3)** — none fails the head:
- **A. Publish re-derivation is conditional.** The materializer runs the reconcile and `declareEveryone` only when the publish materialized at least one row (`applied` above zero) and the published body carries an `isDefault` key. A later publish of an accepted set whose body drops the key entirely is not re-derived until the next boot, accept, revoke or uninstall, although `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` would withhold it ("no longer declares isDefault: true") once asked. The condition is inherited (it gated the reconcile before), and the window is a withdrawal's latency, not a widening; under D5's "no ghost grants" it belongs with the re-home. Escalated to the carrier the dev already names: stage 6b-2 (seat answer 6109520247), which deletes this materializer and re-homes the re-derivation.
- **B. `declareEveryone` never throws.** A confirm whose derivation fails internally still answers 200 with `bindingCreated: false` and an `error` or `warn` line; the record is right and the next derivation converges, and the ablation showed `bindingCreated` carries the signal. Acceptable; the objectui panel should surface `bindingCreated: false` as not-yet-in-force. Carrier: objectui, with flag C.
- **C. Console Pin Gate skipped on this head, correctly.** No pinned-sibling import is removed (the moved symbols are server exports the console never imports), so no pin bump is owed under the Post-Task checklist's rule 4. The behavioural consequences for `SuggestedBindingsPanel` — a caller without `manage_metadata` now gets `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on the list; dismiss on an accepted row revokes — are objectui's, carrier objectui / the C9 lane as the dev filed.

**Out-of-scope findings** — carriers accepted as filed: #22619 for the ADR-0090 D9, ADR-0131 D3 and ADR-0138 section 5 notes; 6a's lane and stage 8 for `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate`; the checklist watchdog for the seven pre-existing `check:platform-checklist` reds on `main`.
